title: Western Blot Protocol for Cell Lysate and Gel Preparation
author: Tyler J Wenzel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sdpea5n
materials: Drug and stimulate cells as desired
Carefully remove lane combs from the upper gel
Place 1 o antibodies back in the stored 50mL conical and freeze for reuse
Add 1mL light ECL reagents (per membrane) and 1mL dark ECL reagent (per membrane) into a 15mL conical Important: Change tips to avoid contaminating ECL reagents)

steps.title: Prepare Cell Lysates
steps.instruction: Seed 2mL of cells at desired density in a 6mL TC-coated petri dish, then extract proteins using RIPA buffer.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells with ice-cold PBS.
Aspirate PBS and add 0.3mL ice-cold RIPA buffer.
Incubate for 5 minutes on ice.
Scrape cells off the dish using a cold plastic cell scraper and transfer to a 0.5mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge samples at 10,000xg for 5 minutes.
Pipette the supernatant into a fresh 1.5mL centrifuge tube and discard the pellet.

steps.title: Cast the Lower Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the lower resolving gel using 1.0mm plates.

substeps.instruction: Clean 1.0mm gel plates with distilled water.
Place plates into a green casting frame and set the frame into the casting stand.
Prepare gel mix (e.g., 8% for 110 kDa proteins); do not add TEMED until ready to pour.
Add TEMED to gel components and immediately pour the lower gel between the plates.
Add 100uL-1mL ethanol over the top of the lower gel until it is even.
Allow the gel to solidify for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Cast the Upper Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the upper stacking gel onto the solidified lower gel.

substeps.instruction: Pour out the ethanol and wash the lower gel once with distilled water.
Pour out distilled water and remove excess water from the edges using the corner of Whatman paper without touching the gel.
Add TEMED to upper gel components and immediately pour over the lower gel until overflowing.
Immediately insert 1.0mm lane combs, ensuring no bubbles are present.
Allow the upper gel to solidify for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Samples and Run Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare protein samples and run the electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Wash the gel once with distilled water by causing it to overflow out of the casting frame.
Move plates to a clamping frame and place in a gel running box.
Fill the box with 1x Laemmli running buffer just below the top of the plates; aspirate any bubbles.
Boil ladder (11uL Biotin ladder mixed with 11uL Opti Marker ladder) in a water bath for 2 minutes.
Boil proteins in a heating block containing water at 90°C for 4 minutes.
Add 10uL of sample to each gel lane (adjust volume based on a standard curve to avoid saturation).
Run the gel at 160V (3.00A) at room temperature until the dye front runs off the bottom (approx. 1h 20min).

steps.title: Assemble Transfer Sandwich
steps.instruction: Construct the gel sandwich for protein transfer to a nitrocellulose membrane.

substeps.instruction: Assemble the sandwich in the following order (black side to clear side): Black sponge, White sponge, 1 piece Whatman paper, Gel, Nitrocellulose membrane (writing face down), 1 piece Whatman paper.
Gently roll out air bubbles using a roller or 50mL conical tube.
Add 2 pieces of Whatman paper, White sponge, and Black sponge.
Roll out air bubbles firmly.

steps.title: Perform Protein Transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins from the gel to the membrane using a transfer box.

substeps.instruction: Seal the sandwich and place it in the transfer box (black side of sandwich facing black side of box).
Add an ice pack to the transfer box and surround the box with packed ice.
Fill the transfer box with 1x Towbin transfer buffer.
Run the transfer at a current of 0.30A for 1h 15min (adjust voltage to achieve this current).

steps.title: Stain and Wash Membrane
steps.instruction: Visualize transfer efficiency and clean the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Move the membrane to a small Tupperware box and Ponceau stain to visualize proteins.
Capture an image of stained proteins using an 18-70mm lens.
Wash the membrane 3 times on a shaker with TBS-T for 5 minutes each to remove Ponceau stain until no color remains.

steps.title: Block and Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Block the membrane and incubate with the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Add Blocking Solution (5% w/v Skim Milk Powder in TBS-T) to the Tupperware box and shake for 1 hour.
Pour off excess Blocking Solution.
Add primary antibody dissolved in blocking solution (typically 1:1000 dilution) and shake overnight at 4°C (alternatively, 1 hour at room temperature for less clear bands).

steps.title: Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane and incubate with the secondary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Wash the membrane with TBS-T at room temperature for 1 hour on a shaker, refreshing the TBS-T every 10 minutes.
Add secondary antibody dissolved in blocking solution and shake at room temperature for 1 hour.
Wash the membrane again with TBS-T at room temperature for 1 hour on a shaker, refreshing TBS-T every 10 minutes.

steps.title: Chemiluminescent Detection
steps.instruction: Apply ECL solution and image the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Dry the membrane in Saran wrap and place in a new Tupperware container.
Using a 1mL pipette, add 2mL ECL solution drop by drop until the membrane is covered.
Cover the box with aluminum foil for 5 minutes.
Take a picture using a chemiluminescent machine at 70mm using the 18-70mm lens, adjusting the aperture ring or machine settings for correct exposure.
